clearedSpotChecks.check: L-781: v3 style swaps produced by the closed validator on the 512 bit branch of FullMath.mulDiv, multi-step groups not yet run (stage B of v3check.py, 7 of the swaps did not reproduce).
clearedSpotChecks.note: The text contradicts itself. It says 0 of the 7 mismatches are explained by the 0xd78218c0 Mint variant and also says chkmis.py was never run on them, and out/stageB-rest.json.part and out/stageB-partial.json hold no mismatch records ("mismatches": []), so the 7 cannot be examined from the saved output. The leadResults entry calls the same work inconclusive, so it should not stand as a cleared item. I reran v3check_rest.py unchanged except for keeping the first 2,500 sampled groups (cycles/017/hyperevm.verify.work/v3first.py, out/stageB-first2500.json). Stage A gave the same 2,258,337 swaps and 121,167 groups as the original log, but the sample differs from the author's (seed not recorded), so these are not the same 7 swaps. 2,612 swaps reproduced, 1,409 of them on the 512 bit mulDiv branch, and 2 did not: tx 0x000afdd9...f434 (block 50505119) and tx 0xabf0dcaa...3596 (block 51001977), both in pool 0x0d3e8f69...16b7. chkmis.py on the archive client (out/chkmis.log) shows that once the unread 0xd78218c0 Mint variant of the same block is applied, the liquidity before each swap equals the logged liquidity exactly (18056408451067369 and 15664874739171611). Both mismatches are therefore collector gaps, as all 4 of cycle 15 were, and neither points to validator output that differs from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116. The conclusion probably holds, but the author's 7 swaps are still unexamined and the item should be recorded as inconclusive.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-185: is there a block in which one transaction leaves sync(ERC-20) without a settle and a later transaction makes a native settle with value?
clearedSpotChecks.note: The code path matches what the item says. sync needs no lock and writes the synced currency and reserves to transient slots (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38). _settle credits the balance rise since that sync, or msg.value when no currency is synced, and reverts on value while an ERC-20 is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). A sync that leaked across transactions would therefore let a later settle be credited with a rise someone else paid. The mined search found no such pair (out/l185.json: 2,782 transactions, no transaction that ends with an ERC-20 synced). Earlier cleared items cover the per transaction reset from the replay clients' source. I added a check of my own: eth_simulateV1 on the archive client rpc.purroofgroup.com with TSTORE(0,0x42) in one call and TLOAD(0) in a later call returned 0, both in the same simulated block and in the next block. A control that stores and loads within one call returned 0x42 (cycles/017/hyperevm.verify.work/tsim.py, out/tsim.json, out/tsim_control.json). The official node and the testnet node answer Method not found to eth_simulateV1, so this added check covers the archive client only.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-548 on HyperEVM: an EIP-7702 designator pointing at each read precompile 0x0800 to 0x0814, called from the PoolManager address.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The premise that 7702 delegated accounts cannot exist holds. The HyperEVM developer page I fetched says the HyperEVM uses the Cancun hardfork without blobs. On chain, at block 0x31c8b15 on both the official node and the archive client, the EIP-2935 history contract 0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935 and the EIP-7002 contract 0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002 have no code, and a call to 0x0b (the BLS12-381 G1ADD precompile from Prague) with empty input returns empty success where Prague would fail. That is consistent with no Prague and so no type 4 transactions. The saved out/probe7702_tx.txt shows -32003 transaction type not supported. That came from an eth_sendRawTransaction attempt by the research agent, not from a read-only query, and I did not repeat it. The code consequence (take moves nothing but debits the caller, src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) only touches the caller's own delta, so a victim who did nothing unusual is not affected. If an upgrade activates Prague, the item must be reopened, as item 12 of the research file says.
